attack_surface_rules.lease: the wrapper takes the canonical local-runtime flock itself before any version probe/snapshot and releases it only after its own cleanup; a busy lease is waited max 90s then status=not_run (exit 2). No --skip flag, no env/UNDER_LOCK bypass; a busy lock is never treated as own.
attack_surface_rules.refusal: a negative authorization assertion only passes for a classified peer close/reset (EOF/reset/broken pipe/proxy 5xx) within 5s while the same client-core pid+starttime stays alive and its local SOCKS port still accepts. Timeout/dead client core/unreachable SOCKS/unclassified error = not_proven and fails.
attack_surface_rules.identity: own scope (any process/config under this run's temp root) must be empty after cleanup; every pre-existing protected original process must still match pid+starttime+exe+cwd+args and every pre-existing TCP/UDP listener must keep its inode. A vanished original is an ENV isolation violation requiring an explicit creator/lease receipt and a re-run; it is never silently ignored as host churn.

exclusions: synthetic usage writes or SQL-fabricated target results
